seguridad.title: Security
seguridad.subtitle: Your organization's authentication policy. These settings affect every user in the tenant.
seguridad.loadError: Could not load the MFA policy.
seguridad.updateError: Could not update the policy. Try again.
seguridad.currentStatusDesc: On the Community plan, MFA is mandatory for administrative roles (super_admin, tenant_admin) and optional for everyone else. The tenant-wide policy lets you enforce MFA for all users.
seguridad.policyDesc: This affects ALL current users in the tenant (students included). They get the configured grace period to enable MFA before their login is blocked.
seguridad.requireAllHelp: While this is active and the Enterprise license remains valid, any user without MFA configured outside the grace period will get a 401 when signing in and will be sent to the MFA setup flow.
seguridad.gracePeriodHelp: Applies from the moment the policy is saved. Once the deadline passes, users without MFA cannot sign in until they set it up.
seguridad.upsellDesc: Enforcing MFA for every user in the tenant is part of the Didacta Enterprise security package. Your current plan (community) already requires MFA for administrators; with Enterprise you can extend it to students, trainers and managers with a configurable grace period.
seguridad.upsellCapability: The required capability is <chip>feat:mfa.enforcement</chip>. If your Enterprise license expires or is revoked, enforcement is disabled automatically — the saved configuration stays dormant until you renew.

sso.noToken: Session has no token. Sign in again.
sso.statusDisabledDesc: There is a saved configuration but it is disabled — the flow is not offered.

oidc.title: SSO with OpenID Connect
oidc.subtitle: Lets your users sign in with their corporate identity (Okta, Azure AD, Auth0, Google Workspace, Keycloak…). Once configured, a “Sign in with SSO” button appears on the tenant's login screen.
oidc.loadError: Could not load the OIDC configuration.
oidc.probeMissingIssuer: Paste the issuer URL before testing.
oidc.probeError: Could not test the IdP discovery.
oidc.deleteConfirm: Delete the SSO configuration? Users will immediately stop being able to sign in with SSO.
oidc.statusEnabledDesc: The SSO button will appear on /signin and users will be able to sign in with their corporate IdP.
oidc.statusEmptyDesc: You have not configured an IdP yet. Start by pasting the issuer URL below.
oidc.idpConfigDesc: You need to have registered an “OpenID Connect / Web” application in your IdP. Paste the callback URL below into its configuration as an authorized redirect URI.
oidc.enableHelp: Shows the “Sign in with SSO” button on /signin for this tenant.
oidc.issuerHelp: Must be HTTPS (http://localhost is accepted for dev). We concatenate it with /.well-known/openid-configuration to discover the endpoints.
oidc.clientSecretHelp: Encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. Min 16 characters when set.
oidc.allowedDomainsHelp: Empty = any email from the IdP is accepted. If you list domains, the callback rejects emails outside those domains even if the IdP authenticated them.
oidc.autoProvisionHelp: When active, the first login automatically creates the account with the student role. When off, only users that already exist in the tenant can sign in (provisioned via SCIM or manually).
oidc.callbackHelp: Set it in the IdP as the “Redirect URI” / “Authorized redirect URI”. If your API sits behind a proxy with a different public domain, override it with the OIDC_REDIRECT_URI env var.
oidc.guideDesc: Generic steps that apply to most IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Auth0, Google Workspace, Keycloak). Field names may vary slightly.
oidc.guideStep1Title: 1. Create the OIDC app in the IdP
oidc.guideStep1Desc: Application type: Web or OIDC Web Application. Authorization Code Flow with PKCE.
oidc.guideStep2Desc: Paste the callback URL (the one above) into the Sign-in redirect URIs / Authorized redirect URIs field.
oidc.guideStep3Desc: Paste the IdP's issuer URL above (without /.well-known), plus the clientId / clientSecret the IdP generates. For Okta the issuer is https://'{'your-org'}'.okta.com/oauth2/default. For Azure AD: https://login.microsoftonline.com/'{'tenant'}'/v2.0.
oidc.guideStep4Desc: Click “Test discovery” — it should respond with the endpoints. If it fails, check that the issuer is HTTPS and reachable from the server.
oidc.guideStep5Desc: Toggle “Enable SSO” → save → click “Try the flow”. It redirects you to the IdP and brings you back signed in.
oidc.guideNoteTitle: Note: limited scope in this pilot
oidc.guideNoteDesc: 1 IdP per tenant, Authorization Code + PKCE only, no role mapping from the IdP. Automatically provisioned users get the student role; admins change it later in Users.
oidc.upsellDesc: Single Sign-On with OpenID Connect is part of the Didacta Enterprise package. It lets your users sign in to Didacta with their corporate identity from Okta, Azure AD, Auth0, Google Workspace, Keycloak or any OIDC-compatible IdP.
oidc.upsellCapability: The required capability is feat:sso.oidc. Without Enterprise, the /admin/sso/oidc/* endpoints return 402 Payment Required and federated login flows do not start.
oidc.error402: This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the `feat:sso.oidc` capability.

saml.title: SSO with SAML 2.0
saml.subtitle: Lets your users sign in with their corporate identity using SAML 2.0 (Okta, Azure AD, Auth0, OneLogin, ADFS, Keycloak…). Once configured, a “Sign in with SSO” button appears on the tenant's login screen.
saml.loadError: Could not load the SAML configuration.
saml.probeMissing: Fill in the IdP's SSO URL and certificate before testing.
saml.probeError: Could not validate the SAML connection.
saml.deleteConfirm: Delete the SAML SSO configuration? Users will immediately stop being able to sign in with SSO.
saml.statusEnabledDesc: The SAML SSO button will appear on /signin and users will be able to sign in with their corporate IdP.
saml.statusEmptyDesc: You have not configured an IdP yet. Start by pasting the details below.
saml.spTitle: SP details (Didacta) to configure in the IdP
saml.spDesc: Paste these values into the IdP panel when you create the SAML application.
saml.spMetadataLabel: Metadata URL (optional, for IdPs that import metadata)
saml.idpConfigDesc: Paste the IdP's Entity ID, SSO endpoint URL and X.509 certificate (PEM). If your IdP supports “download metadata”, open that XML and copy the values of entityID, SingleSignOnService Location and X509Certificate.
saml.enableHelp: Shows the “Sign in with SSO” button on /signin.
saml.entityIdHelp: Unique identifier of the IdP. You will find it as entityID in the metadata.
saml.ssoUrlHelp: URL Didacta redirects to in order to start the SAML login. Must be HTTPS (http://localhost is accepted for dev).
saml.certHelp: The IdP's public certificate. It is used to validate the signature of SAMLResponses — without this cert, no login is accepted.
saml.attrDesc: Every IdP names its attributes differently. The defaults cover Okta / Azure AD / ADFS.
saml.allowedDomainsHelp: Empty = any email from the IdP is accepted. If you list domains, the ACS rejects emails outside those domains even if the IdP authenticated them.
saml.autoProvisionHelp: When active, the first login automatically creates the account with the student role. When off, only users that already exist in the tenant can sign in.
saml.upsellDesc: Single Sign-On with SAML 2.0 is part of the Didacta Enterprise package. It lets your users sign in to Didacta with their corporate identity from Okta, Azure AD, Auth0, OneLogin, ADFS, Keycloak or any SAML-compatible IdP.
saml.upsellCapability: The required capability is feat:sso.saml. Without Enterprise, the /admin/sso/saml/* endpoints return 402 Payment Required and federated login flows do not start.
saml.error402: This feature requires an Enterprise plan with the `feat:sso.saml` capability.

wordpress.title: SSO from WordPress
wordpress.subtitle: Lets users already signed in to your WordPress enter Didacta without signing in again. Your WordPress signs a short-lived token (HMAC) and Didacta verifies it with the shared secret. All the config is stored encrypted — nothing in environment variables.
wordpress.loadError: Could not load the WP-SSO configuration.
wordpress.deleteConfirm: Delete the WP-SSO configuration? Users will stop being able to sign in with WordPress.
wordpress.notAllowed: Only administrators (super_admin / tenant_admin) can configure WordPress SSO.
wordpress.statusEnabledDesc: Active: users with a session on your WordPress can enter without logging in.
wordpress.statusDisabledDesc: There is a saved configuration but it is disabled.
wordpress.statusEmptyDesc: You have not configured WP-SSO yet. Fill in the form below.
wordpress.formDesc: Install the didacta-sso plugin on your WordPress and define the secret and the callback URL below in wp-config.php.
wordpress.secretPlaceholder: the same one as in wp-config.php
wordpress.secretHelp: Same value as DIDACTA_SSO_SECRET in WordPress. Encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM). Min 16 characters. Generate one with openssl rand -hex 32.
wordpress.issuerHelp: Must match your WordPress home_url EXACTLY (it is the auto-bounce destination and the expected token issuer).
wordpress.autoRedirectHelp: Didacta's login bounces to your WordPress; if there is a session, the user comes back authenticated without touching anything. If not, it silently returns to the normal login.
wordpress.autoCreateHelp: When active, the first SSO creates the account (student role). When off, only users that already exist in the tenant can enter.
wordpress.callbackHelp: In WordPress: define('DIDACTA_SSO_CALLBACK', '…') with this URL (it includes your tenant identifier).

smtp.title: Notifications · SMTP
smtp.subtitle: Outgoing server for transactional emails (account activation, password reset, course notifications). If not configured, the tenant inherits the host's global SMTP (if the operator exposed one via env).
smtp.loadError: We could not load the SMTP configuration. Retry.
smtp.saved: Configuration saved. Send a test email to verify it arrives.
smtp.saveError: We could not save the configuration.
smtp.testSent: Test email sent to {email}. Check your inbox.
smtp.testError: We could not send the test email.
smtp.deletedFallback: Configuration deleted. The tenant now uses the host's global SMTP.
smtp.deletedNoFallback: Configuration deleted. Without SMTP no emails are sent — save a new one.
smtp.deleteError: We could not delete the configuration.
smtp.secureHelp: Enable if your provider uses STARTTLS/SSL. ON by default; ports 25 and 587 without encryption are disabled.
smtp.passwordUnchangedPlaceholder: •••••• (leave it empty to keep the current one)
smtp.testDialogDesc: We will use the saved configuration to send an email to the address you provide. If it arrives, we mark the config as verified.
smtp.deleteDialogDesc: You are about to delete the credentials saved for this tenant. If the host has a global SMTP exposed via env, the tenant falls back to it; otherwise emails stop being sent until you save a new configuration.
smtp.bannerUnverified: Configured but unverified — use the Send test email button to confirm delivery.
smtp.bannerFallback: Using the host's global SMTP (fallback). If you want your own sender, save a tenant configuration.
smtp.bannerNone: No SMTP configured — emails (activation, password reset, notifications) are not sent.

emails.title: Platform emails
emails.subtitle: Customize the subject and body of every email the platform sends. If you do not customize one, the product's default text is used. The outgoing (SMTP) server is configured in <link>Settings → Notifications</link>.
